chunks: Then he came before his people in all pomp; and those enamoured of this world, said: "Ah would that we had what Qarun has been given! He indeed possesses great good fortune."

key_terms.الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا: The worldly life, referring to temporal existence and its pleasures
key_terms.حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ: Great share or fortune, indicating a large portion of worldly goods
key_terms.زِينَتِهِ: His adornment or splendor, specifically referring to his wealth and display
key_terms.قَارُونُ: Qarun (Korah), a contemporary of Prophet Musa known for his immense wealth

ai.seo_question: What did Qarun's people say when he appeared in his splendor?
ai.summary: This verse captures the moment Qarun emerges in his full splendor, serving as a focal point for the envy of those attached to worldly life. In Shia exegesis, this display is often interpreted not merely as ostentation but as a manifestation of divine favor (fadilah) that was ultimately wasted due to his arrogance and lack of gratitude. The reaction of his people underscores the universal human struggle between material allure and spiritual contentment.
